title: Reduce the sufficient full-orthant character escape test to real algebra without claiming necessity
statement: For full orthant and reaction polynomials P_r(u)=u^z_r-u^y_r, an escaping sequence ||u_n||->infinity with sum|P_r(u_n)|^2->0 is a sufficient zero-gap certificate via the accepted character quotient. Replacing complex coordinates by their moduli preserves escape and gives ||u|^z_r-|u|^y_r|<=|u^z_r-u^y_r|. Thus complex phases do not strengthen this particular test, which has a real polynomial formulation decidable by quantifier elimination. The necessity for arbitrary zero-gap form-domain sequences is unproved, and proper-class projection adds a separate issue. Effective semilinearity of classes is an imported representation claim, not a coercivity/completeness theorem. Dovetailing the finite-support/cut/character tests with known positive subclasses does not produce a uniform terminating full classifier.
